nodes.summary: An admixture graph on the nodes `V` (Patterson et al. 2012): a rooted directed acyclic graph in which every non-root node has one or two parents, with admixture proportions.
nodes.title: Admixture graph

nodes.summary: The drift model of an admixture graph: the populations are the nodes, the root frequency is `root`, the edge increments are `incr` (square integrable and pairwise uncorrelated), the drift length of an edge is the second moment of its increment, and the weights are the lineage weights of the graph.
nodes.title: Drift model of an admixture graph

nodes.summary: The edges `(child, parent)` of the graph.
nodes.title: Edges of an admixture graph

nodes.summary: With no drift on the admixture edges, an admixture node `X` with parents `A ≠ B` and proportion `α = prop X A` has `f3 X A B = -α (1 - α) f2 A B` (the hypothesis of the seed's `DriftModel.f3_admixture`, here derived from the graph).
nodes.title: Three-population statistic at an admixture node without edge drift

nodes.summary: The three-population statistic at an admixture node `X` with parents `A ≠ B`, proportions `α = prop X A` and `β = prop X B` (`α + β = 1`), in a drift model with the graph's weights: `f3 X A B = α² ℓ_{XA} + β² ℓ_{XB} - α β f2 A B`, where `ℓ_{XA}`, `ℓ_{XB}` are the drift lengths of the two admixture edges.
nodes.title: Three-population statistic at an admixture node

nodes.summary: The three-population test on a tree-shaped admixture graph: `f3 C A B ≥ 0`.
nodes.title: Three-population test is nonnegative on a tree

nodes.summary: A tree-shaped admixture graph induces a drift model with binary loadings (all weights `0` or `1`).
nodes.title: A tree-shaped admixture graph has binary loadings

nodes.summary: The graph is a tree: no node has two parents.
nodes.title: Tree-shaped admixture graph

nodes.summary: The probability of a root-ward path `[v₀, v₁, …, v_k]`: the product of the proportions `prop vᵢ vᵢ₊₁`.
nodes.title: Probability of a root-ward path in an admixture graph

nodes.summary: First-step equation for `paths`.
nodes.title: First-step equation for root-ward paths

nodes.summary: The root-ward paths from `X`: the lists `[X = v₀, v₁, …, v_k = root]` with each `vᵢ₊₁` a parent of `vᵢ`.
nodes.title: Root-ward paths from a node of an admixture graph

nodes.summary: Admixture proportions are at most `1`.
nodes.title: Admixture proportions are at most one

nodes.summary: Acyclicity: a lineage from a parent `Y` of `X` never passes through `X`.
nodes.title: A lineage from a parent never passes through its child

nodes.summary: On a tree every visit probability is `0` or `1`.
nodes.title: Visit probabilities on a tree are zero or one

nodes.summary: First-step equation for `visit`.
nodes.title: First-step equation for visit probabilities

nodes.summary: Visit probabilities are at most `1`.
nodes.title: Visit probabilities are at most one

nodes.summary: Visit probabilities are nonnegative.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of visit probabilities

nodes.summary: Every lineage reaches the root.
nodes.title: Every lineage reaches the root

nodes.summary: A lineage passes through its own node with probability `1`.
nodes.title: A lineage visits its own node with probability one

nodes.summary: `visit X c` is the probability that the lineage of a gene sampled in `X`, traced toward the root with parents chosen according to the admixture proportions, passes through `c`.
nodes.title: Probability that a lineage passes through a node

nodes.summary: The recursion at an admixture node `X` with parents `A ≠ B`: with `α = prop X A`, `w X = α w A + (1 - α) w B + w₀`, where `w₀` puts weight `α` on the edge `(X, A)`, `1 - α` on `(X, B)` and `0` elsewhere.
nodes.title: Lineage weight recursion at an admixture node

nodes.summary: Path-sum form of the lineage weights (Patterson et al. 2012): `weight X e` is the sum, over the root-ward paths from `X` that traverse `e`, of the products of the admixture proportions along the path.
nodes.title: Path-sum formula for lineage weights

nodes.summary: On a tree every lineage weight is `0` or `1`.
nodes.title: Lineage weights on a tree are zero or one

nodes.summary: First-step recursion for lineage weights: a lineage from `X` traverses `e` either as its first step (if `e` starts at `X`) or after moving to a parent `Y`, chosen with probability `prop X Y`.
nodes.title: First-step recursion for lineage weights

nodes.summary: Lineage weights are at most `1`.
nodes.title: Lineage weights are at most one

nodes.summary: Lineage weights are nonnegative.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of lineage weights

nodes.summary: The recursion at a tree node `X` with the single parent `Y`: `w X = w Y + 1_{(X, Y)}`.
nodes.title: Lineage weight recursion at a tree node

nodes.summary: `weight X e` is the probability that the lineage of a gene sampled in `X` traverses the edge `e = (c, p)`: it reaches `c` and then descends from `p`.
nodes.title: Lineage weight of an edge in an admixture graph

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
